display: I'm a recreation coordinator at a long-term care home in East York, Toronto. I plan weekly programs for about ninety residents: sing-alongs, chair yoga, gardening club and reminiscence sessions.

signals.text: I'm looking for a decent piano, donated or second-hand, for our weekly sing-along. The home's upright has been out of tune for two years.
The home can't fund a piano repair this year, so any piano help has to come as a donation approved through the foundation.
Our volunteer pianist, a retired music teacher, says he'll play every week if I find him a good instrument. Until then I'm making do with a Casio keyboard and a playlist.
I'm trying to put up a memory wall in a hallway for families' photos and keepsakes. Six families are in, but I have no budget, and I'm hunting for cheap second-hand frames.
I want the memory wall up before the holidays and could use hands or donated frames.
I keep a binder of every resident's favourite song and the year they first heard it. I'd like a better way to turn it into playlists and sessions without exposing anyone's details.
I could use more volunteers who can sing, play or just sit and listen for short sessions, because residents tire after about 40 minutes.
I'm saving hard for a condo and feel behind. I have about $41,000 and need roughly $18,000 more, which is realistically a year and a half away.
I sometimes wonder whether I should move to a cheaper city, but my work and my residents are here.
Grief from residents passing is harder than I tell people. I mostly cope by going back to work and running the next activity.
I'm quietly tired and sometimes imagine leaving care work, but I can't picture doing anything else.

October is crowded: a bridesmaid dress fitting in Mississauga, a train to Montreal for my sister's wedding, and family pressure to be home for Thanksgiving. I'm trying to fit it all in on a tight budget.
I'm trying not to adopt a shelter cat before I own a condo, and it isn't going well.

offers.text: I have a Recreation Therapy diploma from Humber College and seven years in long-term care. I can design short, low-fatigue activity programs for older adults.
I run sing-alongs and reminiscence sessions, including for people with dementia. I know how to use familiar songs to bring someone back into the room.
I can show you how to build a personal music-memory system, with favourite song, year first heard and who they danced to it with. It works as a template for care homes or families.
I can coordinate a volunteer list of about thirty people, including a few musicians, and match them to short sessions that suit them.
I keep a list of local community choirs and music students I've called over the years, and I can introduce a choir or student looking for a place to perform.
I can offer a stage and an audience: a weekly Thursday 2 pm sing-along in a main lounge, where visiting musicians are warmly received.
I have a small activity budget of about $400 a month, and I can portable-host with a Bluetooth speaker and a Casio keyboard I carry between floors.
I volunteer Saturdays at an animal shelter and can help with socializing cats and with shelter-side volunteer coordination.
I can talk with someone who works in care, or is losing someone, because I have a lot of practice sitting with grief and then carrying on with the day.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a piano technician. I can assess and tune pianos in institutions, and I sometimes do it at reduced rates for good causes.
catchers.can: I'll check what the foundation can accept as an in-kind service. If it works, I'll connect you with our administrator and our volunteer pianist, and a repair that keeps the home's own piano alive becomes possible.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to assess an upright piano on site in Toronto (East York) and give a written estimate, or do the work for a donation-type arrangement?

catchers.hypo: My family is moving out and we have a decent upright piano we'd like to give to a place where people will actually play it.
catchers.can: I can take it through the foundation's donation approval process and put the instrument in front of a retired music teacher, who has offered to play weekly if the piano is good.
catchers.confirm: Is the piano playable and in tune, or tunable, and can it be delivered to Toronto at your side or with a mover?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired music teacher and I'd like to help find or judge a good second-hand piano for a community space.
catchers.can: Our volunteer pianist is a proud retired high school music teacher. I'd introduce you so that two people who care about the instrument can choose one together.
catchers.confirm: Can you check a piano's action, keys and tuning stability in person before a donation is accepted?

catchers.hypo: I run a small community choir and we want to sing for seniors on weekday afternoons, but we don't know who to ask.
catchers.can: I can fit your choir into the Thursday sing-along series, or into another day if the afternoon works, with songs matched to what residents grew up with.
catchers.confirm: Can your group sing for about 30–40 minutes on a weekday afternoon, with a repertoire of older popular songs?

catchers.hypo: I work with people who have dementia in my family, and I want to build a playlist from the songs my mother loved. Where do I begin?
catchers.can: I can walk you through the method I use: favourite song, year first heard, who they danced to, and how to run a short listening session.
catchers.confirm: Do you want to make music a regular part of your relative's day, and not just a one-off playlist?

catchers.hypo: I have a box of picture frames and some wall hooks and I'd like to donate them to a project that honours older people's stories.
catchers.can: I'd use them for the memory wall in our second-floor hallway, where families bring photos and keepsakes.
catchers.confirm: Are the frames in good condition and can they be dropped off in Toronto, preferably in a mix of standard sizes?

catchers.hypo: I'm a first-time buyer in Toronto who also works in a low-paid caring job. Do you know programs that help with a down payment?
catchers.can: I'm walking this path myself, so I can trade notes honestly. A mortgage broker I've spoken to gave me a realistic target, and I can share what I've learned.
catchers.confirm: Are you earning a care-sector or public-service wage and saving toward a one-bedroom in the Toronto area?

catchers.hypo: My sister's wedding is coming up and I've been told I shouldn't spend on shoes, but I feel bad about it. How do bridesmaids on a budget manage?
catchers.can: My sister is getting married in Montreal in October. I can tell you what's worked for me and who offered to pitch in, and introduce you to second-hand and rental options I came across.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for lower-cost options for a bridesmaid outfit, such as renting, borrowing or second-hand?

catchers.hypo: I'm a care worker who has just lost someone I looked after, and I don't know how to carry on with my shift.
catchers.can: I know that feeling. I can talk with you about it, and about the small routines that help.
catchers.confirm: Are you a care worker or recreation worker who has lost someone in your care recently and needs peer support, not clinical help?

catchers.hypo: I'm an animal-shelter coordinator looking for reliable Saturday volunteers who are good with shy or older animals.
catchers.can: I already volunteer there on Saturdays and I'm good with older or anxious animals. I can share the volunteer list I keep and recommend people who fit.
catchers.confirm: Do you need steady weekend volunteers with some experience of handling cats, in Toronto?

forbids.text: I won't share residents' names, medical information or any detail that could identify them.
Anything for the home goes through the foundation approval process, so I can't accept money, equipment or repairs outside it.
I can't pay for repairs out of my own activity fund.
I work Monday to Friday, 8 to 4, and don't do weekend work for the home without admin approval.
Sessions for residents have to be short, about 40 minutes at most.
I'm not looking to turn residents' stories or songs into marketing or content.

projects.name: Fall Sing-Along Series
projects.text: A weekly Thursday 2 pm sing-along in the main lounge, aimed especially at residents with dementia. The main need is a decent piano and a regular pianist.
roles_needed: someone to judge a second-hand piano

projects.name: Memory Wall
projects.text: A hallway wall for photos and keepsakes that families bring in. Six families are on board; it needs frames, hanging materials and a small budget before the holidays.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share the piano problem, the sing-along program, what the home can and can't do, and how the foundation approval works.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and I know who you are, I'll talk about my own finances, how work grief affects me, and where I'm stuck with admin over the budget.
policy.never: Residents' names, medical information, or anything that could identify an individual resident.
